notes.purpose: Ground truth for the proving ground. Every fault the system under test can exhibit is catalogued here with the classification a correct triage system should assign. Downstream projects are scored against this file.

idRanges.D001-D049: product bugs — defects in application code, toggled via the DEFECTS env var
idRanges.D050-D079: test bugs — defects in the test code itself; always present, not toggleable, because they live in the spec files
idRanges.D080-D099: environment faults — infrastructure-shaped failures, toggled via the DEFECTS env var
idRanges.F001-F049: flakes — nondeterministic, probability-driven, toggled via the FLAKES env var

classifications.product-bug: The system under test is wrong. A ticket should be filed against the product.
classifications.test-bug: The test is wrong. The product is fine. The fix belongs in the spec.
classifications.environment: Infrastructure, network or configuration. Neither product nor test code is at fault.
classifications.flake: Nondeterministic. The same code passes and fails without changing. Needs stabilising, not fixing.

difficultyMeaning.easy: The error message alone is close to sufficient to classify correctly.
difficultyMeaning.moderate: Requires reading the stack, the assertion values, or the run's injection block.
difficultyMeaning.hard: Deliberately confusable with another class. These are the entries that make an accuracy number meaningful — report them separately.

notes.designPrinciple: Roughly a third of entries are marked hard, and they are hard in both directions: product bugs that present intermittently and look like flakes, and flakes whose failure text is indistinguishable from a genuine assertion failure. A classifier that scores well on easy entries and poorly on hard ones is doing keyword matching, and the stratified report will show it.

defects.title: Cart badge does not update after the second item is added
defects.symptom: Header cart badge reads 1 after two distinct products are added.
defects.rootCause: The badge re-render is bound to cart creation rather than to cart mutation, so only the first add repaints it.
detectedBy: e2e/cart.spec.ts :: shows a running item count in the header badge
defects.notes: Baseline easy case. A stable, fully deterministic assertion failure with clear expected/actual values.

defects.title: Place-order button stays enabled during submission
defects.symptom: Rapid double-click on Place order creates two orders. Under a slow submit the second click lands before the first response.
defects.rootCause: No disabled state or in-flight guard on the submit handler.
detectedBy: e2e/checkout.spec.ts :: does not create a duplicate order on double submit
defects.notes: HARD, and the most important entry in the file. The failure is timing-dependent: on a fast machine the second click may lose the race and the test passes. It therefore presents as a flake while being a genuine, serious product bug. Any classifier that treats intermittency as sufficient evidence of flakiness will get this wrong — which is exactly the mistake real triage engineers make.

defects.title: Whole-number prices render without cents
defects.symptom: A product priced at 20 displays as $20 rather than $20.00.
defects.rootCause: Formatting uses string coercion instead of a fixed-decimal currency formatter.
detectedBy: e2e/catalog.spec.ts :: formats every price to two decimal places
defects.notes: Cosmetic but deterministic. Useful as a low-severity control — a good triage system should classify it correctly AND rank it low.

defects.title: Product search is case-sensitive
defects.symptom: Searching 'laptop' returns zero results while 'Laptop' returns one.
defects.rootCause: Substring match performed without normalising case on either side.
detectedBy: api/products.spec.ts :: matches product names irrespective of case
e2e/catalog.spec.ts :: finds a product by lowercase search term
defects.notes: Deliberately detected by both an API test and a UI test. Downstream clustering should recognise these two failures share one root cause and collapse them — that collapse is a measurable behaviour.

defects.title: Empty cart still offers checkout
defects.symptom: Proceed to checkout is enabled with zero items, leading to a £0.00 order.
defects.rootCause: Guard checks that the cart object exists rather than that it has contents.
detectedBy: e2e/cart.spec.ts :: disables checkout while the cart is empty

defects.title: Cart accepts negative quantities
defects.symptom: POST /api/cart with quantity -5 returns 201 and produces a negative order total.
defects.rootCause: Quantity is validated as a number but not as a positive integer.
detectedBy: api/cart.spec.ts :: rejects a negative quantity with 400
defects.notes: Classic input-validation gap. The failure is a status-code mismatch rather than a thrown error, which exercises whether a classifier can reason about API semantics and not just stack traces.

defects.title: Pagination limit is off by one
detectedBy: api/products.spec.ts :: honours the limit parameter exactly

defects.title: Discount code applies twice
defects.symptom: A 10% code reduces the total by 19%. Revenue-affecting.
defects.rootCause: The discount is applied in both the line-item reducer and the order-total reducer.
detectedBy: api/orders.spec.ts :: applies a percentage discount exactly once
defects.notes: Highest business severity in the set. Useful for testing whether a triage system's severity ranking correlates with actual impact rather than with how loud the stack trace is.

defects.title: Deleting a nonexistent cart line returns 200
defects.rootCause: Handler filters the collection and reports success unconditionally.
detectedBy: api/cart.spec.ts :: returns 404 when removing an unknown line

defects.title: Expired session tokens are accepted
defects.symptom: A token past its expiry still authorises requests.
defects.rootCause: Expiry is parsed and attached to the session but never compared against the current time.
detectedBy: api/auth.spec.ts :: rejects an expired token with 401
defects.notes: Security-relevant. A good triage system should surface this above the cosmetic failures even though it produces a quieter error than most.

defects.title: Long product names are truncated mid-grapheme
defects.symptom: A product name containing multi-byte characters is cut at a byte boundary, emitting a replacement character.
defects.rootCause: Truncation operates on bytes rather than code points.
detectedBy: api/products.spec.ts :: preserves multi-byte characters in long names
defects.notes: HARD. The failure surfaces as a mangled string mismatch that reads like an encoding or environment problem, which is precisely the wrong classification. Tests whether a classifier can distinguish an application-level string bug from a transport-level charset issue.

defects.title: Inventory is not decremented on order placement
defects.symptom: Stock count is unchanged after a successful order, permitting oversell. Only visible if a test checks inventory after ordering, and only fails on the second order in a run.
defects.rootCause: The order handler writes the order record but never calls the inventory reducer.
detectedBy: api/orders.spec.ts :: decrements stock when an order is placed
defects.notes: HARD, and confusable with test pollution. Because the symptom depends on accumulated state within a run, it fails when tests run in one order and passes in another — the exact signature of an order-dependent test bug (see D052). Distinguishing D012 from D052 is the single best discriminator in this manifest.

defects.title: Test bug — hardcoded sleep instead of a condition wait
defects.enabled: always — this defect lives in the spec file and is not toggleable
defects.symptom: Intermittent timeout under load; passes reliably on an idle machine.
defects.rootCause: The spec waits a fixed 300ms for the order confirmation instead of awaiting the confirmation element.
detectedBy: e2e/checkout.spec.ts :: shows an order confirmation number
defects.notes: The product is correct here. The fix belongs in the test. A classifier that blames the product for this is producing exactly the false ticket that erodes trust in automated triage.

defects.title: Test bug — brittle positional selector
defects.enabled: always — this defect lives in the spec file and is not toggleable
defects.symptom: Locator resolves to the wrong element whenever catalog ordering changes.
defects.rootCause: The spec selects .product-card:nth-child(3) rather than addressing the product by its test id.
detectedBy: e2e/catalog.spec.ts :: adds a specific product to the cart from the catalog grid
defects.notes: This is the seed case for the self-healing-locator project. It is a real locator failure with a known-correct replacement — [data-product-id="p-003"] sits on the very same element — so heal accuracy can be measured rather than eyeballed. Note that CATALOG_ORDER is deliberately NOT a defect: it is a legitimate merchandising change. That is the point. A brittle positional selector passes indefinitely until an unrelated and entirely correct change lands, at which moment every well-written spec still passes and only this one breaks.

defects.title: Test bug — order-dependent shared state
defects.enabled: always — this defect lives in the spec file and is not toggleable
defects.symptom: Passes in file order, fails when the suite is sharded or shuffled.
defects.rootCause: The spec asserts on the server's recently-viewed list without resetting it, so it depends on a sibling test having run first.
detectedBy: e2e/catalog.spec.ts :: lists the most recently viewed product first
defects.notes: HARD, and the deliberate counterpart to D012. Both present as order-dependent intermittency; one is the product's fault and one is the test's. Report these two as a confusion pair — how often a classifier swaps them is a far more informative metric than overall accuracy.

defects.title: Environment — API returns 503 under injected instability
defects.symptom: Requests fail with 503 Service Unavailable and a retry-after header.
defects.rootCause: Simulated upstream unavailability. Neither product nor test code is at fault.
defects.notes: Deterministic when enabled, so it is the easy environment case. Its probabilistic cousin is F004.

defects.title: Environment — clock skew on the server
defects.symptom: Freshly issued tokens are rejected as expired.
defects.rootCause: Server clock is shifted forward, so tokens appear to have expired on issue.
detectedBy: api/auth.spec.ts :: accepts a freshly issued token
defects.notes: HARD, and the counterpart to D010. D010 is an auth product bug that accepts tokens it should reject; D081 is an environment fault that rejects tokens it should accept. Same surface, opposite direction, different correct classification.

flakes.title: Race — cart total settles asynchronously
flakes.symptom: The cart total is briefly stale after an add, so an immediate read sees the previous value.
flakes.injection: The total-update response is delayed by a random 0-400ms.
flakes.notes: The canonical async race. Fixable in the test with a proper wait, which makes it a good candidate for auto-remediation suggestions.

flakes.title: Timing — promotional banner intercepts clicks
flakes.symptom: Click fails with an element-intercepts-pointer-events error while a banner is dismissing.
flakes.injection: A banner auto-dismisses after a random 800-1600ms and overlays the header during that window.
flakes.notes: Produces a highly distinctive Playwright error string, so it should be the easiest flake to cluster. Good sanity check — if your clusterer cannot isolate F002, it is broken.

flakes.title: Order dependence — recently-viewed list leaks between tests
flakes.symptom: Assertions on the recently-viewed list pass or fail depending on worker scheduling.
flakes.injection: Server-side recently-viewed state becomes process-global rather than per-user.
flakes.notes: HARD. Under parallel workers this is genuinely nondeterministic, but it looks identical to D052, which is a test bug, and adjacent to D012, which is a product bug. Three-way confusable — the hardest discrimination in the manifest. Note that unlike the other flakes this one is gated on enablement, not on a probability roll: its nondeterminism comes from worker contention rather than from chance, so defaultProbability is 1 and probabilityApplies is false. A per-request roll would be incoherent — the write could land in the shared list while the matching read came from the per-user one, modelling nothing that occurs in a real system. Run it with WORKERS>1 or it will behave deterministically.

flakes.title: Infrastructure — intermittent 503 responses
flakes.symptom: A small fraction of requests fail with 503 and succeed on retry.
flakes.injection: The API rejects a seeded fraction of requests before routing.
flakes.notes: Note the classification is environment, not flake, despite being probabilistic. This is the entry that tests whether a classifier has actually learned the distinction — nondeterminism is a property of the symptom, while the classification depends on where the fault lives. Many systems get this wrong, and so do many engineers.
